personas.name: The Delegated Task Shopper
personas.context: Working a storefront on someone else's behalf against an explicit brief: search a generic category, pick the best option, add it to cart, stop before checkout. Knows the category by name but arrives with no product in mind, and works in a browser window narrow enough that the buy box is clipped at the right edge.
goals: Reach one defensible pick without reading ten thousand listings
Keep the path from a search result to a cart as short as possible
Get an unambiguous signal that the item actually landed in the cart
Stay inside the brief and stop exactly where they were told to
frustrations: A shipping and pricing locale is substituted without being asked, and dismissing the banner does not undo it
Pressing Enter opens the suggestion list instead of running the search
Three different authority badges sit on three different products with nothing to rank them against each other
Some listings hide the cart behind a "See options" detour and others do not
The Add to Cart button is off-canvas, and once found it sits beside a Buy Now button that skips checkout entirely
personas.quote: Let me pull the full text of the results to compare more options
grounded_in: Search stalls at the suggestion list
Competing badges replace a ranked answer
Variant picking is a hidden tax

personas.name: The Absent Requester
personas.context: The person the purchase is for, not at the keyboard. Sets the boundary of the task up front — add to cart, do not check out — and reads the outcome afterwards, judging both the pick and whether the boundary held. Learns about anything odd only in the closing summary.
goals: Understand why this item was chosen over the alternatives, not just that it was chosen
Trust that the session stopped where they said it would stop
See the price they would actually pay, in the currency they expect
frustrations: The locale and currency substitution surfaces only after the fact, as a closing flag
The decision about which options were dropped for step count is made before they can weigh in
Fixing the currency is handed back to them as an unstarted task
personas.quote: If you want USD pricing, that'd mean explicitly setting a US delivery address.
grounded_in: Variant picking is a hidden tax

journey.stage: Lands and gets redirected by geography
actions: Opens amazon.com expecting the standard US storefront
Reads a banner announcing items that ship to India
Dismisses the banner to keep browsing
friction: A shipping and pricing context is applied from detected location without being requested
The banner is dismissible but the currency behind it is not — INR persists past the dismissal

journey.stage: Types the query and nothing happens
actions: Clicks into the search field and types the category name
Presses Enter to commit the query
Notices the autocomplete list opened instead of results loading
Clicks their own words back out of the dropdown to finally run the search
friction: Enter does not fire the search from the search field
The shopper has to diagnose that nothing happened before they can recover

actions: Scans the first rows of a grid reporting over 10,000 matches
Spots an Overall Pick on one product and a Best Seller on another
Gives up on comparing inside the grid and pulls the whole result set as text
friction: No single authority signal to defer to — badges compete rather than rank
Prices read in INR on a US storefront, so nothing can be compared against a known budget
Comparing options properly means working outside the interface that was meant to do it

journey.stage: Re-ranks by proof instead of by badge
actions: Weighs review volume and recent purchase counts as the real ranking signal
Discounts premium listings that require a See options detour to reach a cart
Settles on the Crayola set as the best balance of trust and directness
friction: Step count silently vetoes products that were never judged on merit
What each badge actually certifies is never explained, so they are treated as noise

journey.stage: Verifies the product and hunts for the button
actions: Opens the product page and re-confirms rating, badge, and discount
Looks for Add to Cart and finds it cut off at the right edge
Scrolls the element into view, then scrolls right, before the buy box is usable
friction: The one control the whole session exists to reach is outside the viewport
Three recovery moves are needed before the primary action can be clicked
Buy Now sits adjacent to the target and has to be consciously avoided

actions: Clicks Add to Cart and reads the green confirmation banner
Checks the cart badge incremented and the subtotal appeared
Stops before Proceed to checkout, as instructed, and reports the currency oddity back
friction: The substituted currency survives all the way into the subtotal
The locale problem is raised only after the task is done, as a closing note

hmw_statements.statement: We should let people undo a mistake.
hmw_statements.derived_from: Lands and gets redirected by geography

hmw_statements.statement: How might we help a shopper reach one defensible choice without leaving the results in order to compare them?
How might we make competing trust signals mean something a shopper can actually weigh against each other?
hmw_statements.derived_from: Competing badges replace a ranked answer

hmw_statements.statement: How might we keep the effort of reaching a cart from deciding which product wins?
hmw_statements.derived_from: Variant picking is a hidden tax

hmw_statements.statement: How might we make sure the action a shopper came to take is never the hardest one to find?
hmw_statements.derived_from: Verifies the product and hunts for the button
